title.narrative: Supporting water governance based on science for mitigation, adaptation, and res

description.narrative: Iran faces frequent droughts, impacting water availability and agriculture due to prolonged below-average rainfall and rising temperatures. Droughts lead to crop failures, livestock losses, and strain on water resources, affecting drinking water supplies and industrial needs. Prolonged droughts further threaten the environment and socio-economic stability, causing desertification and land degradation. Iran ranks 4th globally for water stress, enduring multi-year droughts that jeopardize water availability across all sectors. Climate change worsens the situation, impacting rainfall patterns and water resources. With over 80% of renewable fresh water already utilized, Iran faces an unprecedented water crisis. Agriculture, relying on over 90% of scarce water resources, faces challenges to food security due to climate change and unsustainable practices, further endangering rural livelihoods. Therefore, Water governance can facilitate adaptation, mitigation and resilience processes considering the human factor, including climate change, impact on the hydrological and nutrient cycles in ecosystems and based on scientific facts. UNESCO will support the country in addressing global complex interlinkages and water challenges by people and institutions having adequate capacity and scientifically based knowledge to make informed decisions on water management to attain sustainable development and to build resilient societies. The activity Contributes to SDGs Goal: 6,5,13, 14, 15, 17.
